note: The gym (`trn`) and the joint (`kos`) handlers of `orig/g.exe`, the half-open image range `1000:e390`..`1000:ea94` -- from the `trn` verb compare through, but not including, the `i` verb compare -- mapped by Task 31 from an aligned decode, never from a screen. Prose twin: `docs/re/gym.md`; re-derived from `orig/g.exe` by `tools/test_gym_arms.py`. `data/den_arms.json` is the shape this follows. COVERAGE BOUNDARY: this artifact covers exactly that range and nothing else. The sweeps in `tools/test_gym_arms.py` (literals, branches, draws, absolute writes, DGROUP addresses, DS pushes, span tiling) are SET EQUALITIES over the range, so an omitted entry reds the test -- but they say nothing about the two routines the range CALLS (`1000:2526`, the level-up, from the gym's `3` arm; `1000:29c4`, the beer sub-dispatcher, from the shared tail at `1000:e966`), whose bodies were not decoded for this task. TWO HANDLERS, ONE FILE: the gym is a modal submenu, `kos` is a one-shot street verb that merely sits next to it in address space. They are kept in separate top-level blocks (`gym`-prefixed keys and `joint`) because the port puts them in different places: the gym becomes a new module, `kos` stays with `Game::smoke`.
address_forms: `1000:xxxx` is a Ghidra label (Form A of `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md`) and, because the game's code segment is the load base, its OFF is also the image offset. `20ae:xxxx` is DGROUP. `0eed:` and `0f78:` are Form B runtime segments. `cs_offset` is the image offset of a Pascal shortstring's LENGTH byte -- the exact immediate of the `mov di,imm16` that pushes it -- and `file_offset` is that plus the 0x18d0-byte MZ header, which is what `data/strings.json` keys on. The two near calls in range encode a `rel16` that WRAPS: `1000:e7df` and `1000:e966` reach `1000:2526` and `1000:29c4` only modulo 64 KiB, which is the mistake `tools/re_derive.py`'s `near_calls_to` exists to avoid.

range.note: Half-open. `1000:e390` IS the `trn` compare; `1000:ea94` IS the `i` compare and is NOT decoded as part of this map. `trn`'s own half is `1000:e390`..`1000:e973` and `kos`'s is `1000:e973`..`1000:ea94`, the split `data/command_dispatch.json` already records.

verb.note: The verb is read out of the STREET buffer `20ae:3972`, not the gym's own `20ae:3a72`; the setup push at `1000:e386` is the evidence. `1000:e386` and `1000:e38b` are before the range start and are recorded here as the left boundary's own setup. A miss jumps to `1000:e961`, which is also where the gym's `w` exit lands -- so the shared tail is on every street line's path, not only the gym's.

bounded_on_the_right_by.note: `1000:ea8a` is the next verb's own buffer push and is where every `kos` exit lands, so the range's right edge is an instruction boundary the handler itself jumps to, not a number picked to fit. `data/command_dispatch.json` records `i`'s compare at `1000:ea94`.

menu_vs_arm_finding.claim: The second block `1000:e633`..`1000:e941` is NOT a second menu tier and NOT a repeat of the first. It is the key dispatch; `1000:e400`..`1000:e594` is the menu print. They share guard CONSTANTS and almost no code.
menu_vs_arm_finding.how_it_is_reached: Fall-through, once: the last menu line's `WriteLn` at `1000:e5df` is followed by the prompt at `1000:e5e4`, the `ReadLn` at `1000:e60b`..`1000:e615`, the case fold at `1000:e61f`, and then the first key compare at `1000:e62e`. longest_common_byte_run.what_it_is: five zeroed `WriteLn` format words (15 bytes), the five-byte `call 0eed:01c2` after them, and a whole five-byte `cmp byte [0x3692],0x1` -- the run stops there because the `jcc` that follows the compare differs (`76 69` in the menu, `77 03` in the arm). Boilerplate every print in the image shares, not a shared body

pairs.difference: byte-identical, 17 bytes; only the `jcc` after them differs, and it differs in SENSE because the menu skips the row where the arm proceeds

16 bytes against 21. The first five (`a0 92 36 30 e4`, `mov al,[0x3692]` / `xor ah,ah`) and the last nine (`8b d0 a0 34 3e 30 e4 3b c2`) are identical and in the same order. In between the menu has `d1 e0` (`shl ax,1`, so district*2) and the arm has `48 48 ba 0a 00 f7 e2` (`dec ax` / `dec ax` / `mov dx,0xa` / `mul dx`, so (district-2)*10). That two-bytes-against-seven substitution IS the whole difference, and it is a different NUMBER, not a different spelling of the same one.

gates_the_menu_does_not_have.what: `cmp byte [0x394a],0x0` -- already owns the tooth guard. Row 4's only menu gate is district > 1, so the row stays listed after the purchase and the arm refuses it.

menu_vs_arm_finding.the_price_test_has_two_different_ROLES: In the menu the money compare is COSMETIC: both of its arms fall into the same string assembly and only the colour byte `20ae:3b7a` differs (`1000:e407` stores `'0'`, `1000:e40e` stores `'4'`). No menu row is ever HIDDEN by price. In the arms the identical compare is a refusal that skips the whole effect block. Same five bytes, different consequence -- and a port that shares one helper between them would either hide unaffordable rows or charge for nothing.
menu_vs_arm_finding.note: `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md`: symmetry is a hypothesis, not a finding. The hypothesis here was 'the second block repeats the first's guards'. Measured: eight of the ten guard constants ARE byte-identical, one predicate is byte-identical, one predicate is a different number, and one arm carries a gate the menu has no counterpart for. Only the last two matter to a port, and neither would have been found by reading the constants.

joint.port_status: PORTED IN FULL by `Game::smoke`. `grep -n 'fn smoke' src/game.rs` finds it and `grep -n '1000:e9b8' src/game.rs` finds the countdown citation. All four of its branches read `port_touched: false` in `data/branches.json` because that column is a CITATION proxy over `src/**/*.rs` (`data/branches.json`'s own `port_cross_reference.metric` says so), and `src/game.rs` cites the guard `1000:e97d` but not `1000:e978`, `1000:e9a5`, `1000:e9af` or `1000:e9d5`. port_equivalences.why_equivalent: the two are written and cleared together and never independently: `grep -n 'stoned' src/game.rs src/persist.rs` finds the setter in `Game::smoke`, the clear in `Game::wander_preamble` when the countdown hits 0, and `stoned: save.buff_countdown != 0` on load, so a loaded save cannot desynchronise them

`Fighter::joints` is `u16` (`grep -n 'pub joints' src/model.rs`), so the negative half of the signed test is unrepresentable and `== 0` and `<= 0` decide the same way. A future change of that field to a signed type would break the equivalence, which is why it is written down rather than assumed

port_equivalences.original: 1000:e97d -- `cmp byte [0x38b0],0x1` / `jnz`, so the arm runs iff the BYTE is not 1
port_equivalences.port: `self.player.broken_jaw`, a bool, refusing iff it is true
port_equivalences.why_equivalent: the same shape of argument as the `u16 joints` entry below: the byte only ever holds 0 or 1, so `!= 1` and `== 0` decide alike. All five image-wide writers store one of those two -- `1000:47ee` and `1000:4820` store 1, `1000:5031`, `1000:b2ae` and `1000:d558` store 0 -- and `python3 tools/re_query.py xrefs-to 20ae:38b0` is the command that recomputes the set. A writer storing 2 would make the original run the arm and the port refuse it

when hp > hpmax the original's ax is negative, `jnl` fails and it takes the top-up branch, which LOWERS hp to hpmax; `saturating_sub` gives 0, which is also < 10, so the port takes the same branch and makes the same assignment

port_reachability.claim: No arm of the gym is unreachable in this port for want of a writer: every global a gym or joint gate reads is written somewhere in `src/`.
port_reachability.tier: flow for the original addresses; the port half cites the command that recomputes it, per `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md`

one_exception.what: The `5` arm's ceiling reads a value this port does not have. `Game::imm_row_visible` substitutes `armor` for it, which is the standing `docs/re/gaps.md` entry, and the ARM would need the same value against a DIFFERENT threshold. The four flags it is computed from ARE all writable in play as of Task 26 (`grep -n 'wear_suit_abibas_38b4 = true' src/game.rs`), so nothing blocks computing it -- this is missing code, not a missing input.

port_reachability.note: This is the answer to 'unreachable in this port': nothing here is dead for lack of a setter, and unlike the den there is no `FUN_1000_3d11` parameter to block anything -- the gym calls out exactly twice, to the level-up and to the beer sub-dispatcher, and both are already ported.

what_the_port_must_change.what: `Game::shop_turn` recognises NO gym key. Five exist and are established at compare addresses on the gym's own buffer: `1` (`1000:e62e`), `2` (`1000:e6ba`), `3` (`1000:e73c`), `4` (`1000:e7f3`), `5` (`1000:e875`). `w` (`1000:e93c`) is already handled by the shared exit arm. Verify with `grep -n 'Location::Gym' src/game.rs`: today the only matches are the prompt, the intro, the discovery line and the wander/den reveals -- no key arm.

Arm `1`'s damage split. `1000:e68d` `jnz` skips exactly four bytes, and `1000:e68f inc [0x38a8]` is exactly four bytes long, so `урон min` rises only when the NEW strength is even while `урон max` (`1000:e693`) rises every time. Both-conditional and both-unconditional are equally wrong and equally invisible in a screen capture; assert them separately, e.g. buy twice from an odd starting strength and require `dmg_min` +1 and `dmg_max` +2.

Arm `3` is the port's only new draw source in this range. The sequence is: `money -= 10` (`1000:e796`), `xp += 10` (`1000:e7b4`), PRINT the `+10 качков опыта` line (`1000:e7ce`, whose one `#` is filled from a separate `mov ax,0xa` at `1000:e7be` pushed at `1000:e7c1`, not from the xp total), and only THEN the level-up. In `crate::progress::apply_levels` terms that is `progress.xp += 10` and a later call with `award = 0, uncapped = false`, because `apply_levels` adds its own award before the threshold test. Passing `award = 10` to a call made after the manual `xp += 10` would double the grant.

Arm `5` needs the trained-armour value `20ae:3e34`, and needs it against `(district - 2) * 10` (`1000:e87f`..`1000:e894`) -- NOT against `district * 2`, which is the MENU row's threshold (`1000:e57d`..`1000:e58d`). The two predicates differ by exactly `d1 e0` against `48 48 ba 0a 00 f7 e2`; everything else in them is byte-identical. Sharing one helper between the row and the arm is the mistake this entry exists to prevent. The arm must also raise BOTH `armor` (`1000:e8d6`) and the scratch (`1000:e8da`), or it never stops.

Arm `4` refuses when the guard is already owned (`1000:e7fa`), and the MENU row has no such gate (`1000:e51a` is its only one). So after the purchase the row is still listed and the key still prints `^6У тебя есть эта штучка.` -- do not 'fix' the menu.

The menu prints once, on entry (`1000:e400`..`1000:e5e4`), and the loop's back edge `1000:e943` returns to the PROMPT. An unrecognised key is silent -- there is no `Непонятно` string in the range for it to print. `Game::shop_turn`'s catch-all already behaves this way; recorded so a porting task does not add a message.

At district 1 the keys `3`, `4` and `5` are not compared at all (`1000:e728`, `1000:e7e2`, `1000:e861` jump over the compares), so typing `3` there is silent rather than refused. A port that compares the key first and checks the district second would print a refusal the original has no path to.

`kos` needs NO change. `Game::smoke` reproduces all four gates and all seven effects; `joint.port_equivalences` records the three places the port's representation differs from the original's and why each is equivalent. The four `port_touched: false` branches are missing CITATIONS, not missing behaviour.

The gym's own `ReadLn` does not trim (`0eed:0216` at `1000:e61f` only lowercases). `Game::shop_turn` trims; `docs/re/gaps.md`'s trimmed-prompt entry already owns that divergence and this map adds the gym to its population rather than opening a new one.

known_not_boundaries.note: Addresses this artifact NAMES but does not claim are instruction boundaries reachable from a function entry. `tools/test_gym_arms.py` exempts exactly these from the boundary walk AND asserts each really is outside it, so the exemption cannot smuggle in a wrong address. Each entry also names the instruction that COVERS it and the byte index it falls at, and both are re-derived from the aligned decode -- fix round 1 found the prose here asserting a byte role the binary contradicts (`1000:e594` called the LAST byte of a two-byte `jl` whose next instruction is at `1000:e596`), which is exactly the authored-prose surface no other check in `tools/test_gym_arms.py` reached. `inside`/`byte_index` are the executable replacement; `why` no longer carries the byte arithmetic on its own.

entries.why: the half-open END of `menu_vs_arm_finding.menu_span`. It falls inside the row-5 colour branch `1000:e594 jl 0xe59d`, whose opcode byte is `1000:e594` and whose rel8 is `1000:e595`; the next boundary is `1000:e596`.

the half-open END of `menu_vs_arm_finding.arm_span`. It falls inside the `w` hit branch `1000:e941 jz 0xe946`, whose opcode byte is `1000:e941` and whose rel8 is `1000:e942`; the next boundary is `1000:e943`, the miss `jmp`.

spans_note: These 21 spans tile `1000:e390`..`1000:ea94` end to end with no gap and no overlap, which is what stops a block being dropped from the map by being left out of every span. `tools/test_gym_arms.py` asserts the tiling and that every boundary is an aligned instruction start.

sweeps.note: The anchors `tools/test_gym_arms.py` asserts SET EQUALITY against. Each is a count over the aligned decode of `1000:e390`..`1000:ea94`; a wrong count reds the sweep, which is the point -- an inventory guarded by nothing is the defect `docs/re/METHODOLOGY.md` names.
sweeps.random_call_sites_note: ZERO. The gym and the joint spend no `Random` draw of their own. The `3` arm can still move the stream, through `1000:2526`, which spends two draws per level gained at `1000:25fe` -- so 'no draws in range' is not 'no draws'.

branch_census.note: Reproduced from `data/branches.json` at this commit, not copied from the task brief. `port_touched` is a CITATION proxy over `src/**/*.rs` -- `data/branches.json`'s `port_cross_reference.metric` says so in as many words -- so 'untouched' means 'no address citation', never 'unimplemented'.
branch_census.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
B=json.load(open('data/branches.json'))['branches']
off=lambda a:int(a.split(':')[1],16)
for n,lo,hi in (('trn',0xe390,0xe972),('kos',0xe973,0xea93)):
    r=[b for b in B if lo<=off(b['addr'])<=hi]
    print(n,len(r),'branches,',

EOF
branch_census.the_briefs_numbers_are_a_different_measu: Task 31's brief says 23 of 38 and 3 of 5 untouched. Neither is the `port_touched` column: that gives 37 and 4. The brief's pair is reproduced by a DIFFERENT rule -- scan `src/*.rs` for `1000:xxxx` citations and count a branch as touched when its own address OR its guard's address appears -- which is the rule `docs/re/branches.md`'s wander cross-check block uses. Both numbers are right about different questions; recorded so a later reader does not 'correct' one into the other.
